To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed and fabricated an intermediate layer (IL) for organic tandem solar cells using a simple solution processing technique.
the use of silver nanoparticles in the intermediate layer of a tandem solar cell can enhance the efficiency of the device.
the use of Ag-NP and GQD in the IML enhances the recombination process and hence the efficiency of the organic tandem solar cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and fabrication process of an IML for tandem solar cell using solution process.
the development of a simple solution process to fabricate an efficient IML using Ag-NPs of different sizes and GQDs for efficient organic tandem solar cells.
the fabrication of an efficient intermediate layer (IM) using silver and graphene-quantum dots (GQDs) for homo-tandem cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of Ag-NP in IML enhances the performance of tandem cells.
the use of Ag-NP embedded IMLs has a positive effect on the performance of the homo-tandem solar cells.
, the incorporation of Ag-NPs and GQD in the IML is an efficient way to achieve high performance tandem solar cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ag-NPs and graphene quantum dots (GQDs) embedded IMLs have a great potential to be used as an effective IML for organic tandem solar cells.
the use of Ag-NP embedded IML in tandem solar cells is an efficient way to enhance the recombination process in the device.
the use of Ag-NP embedded IML in tandem devices is highly effective in improving the efficiency of the tandem device.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Ag-NPs of 7 nm size embedded in the IML of tandem cells can be used to achieve higher efficiency.
the Ag-NPs embedded IML is a promising candidate for the fabrication of efficient tandem solar cells.
the use of Ag-NP embedded IMLs in tandem devices is a promising approach for improving the device performance.
